brief.scope: Review only GPT-6 C2 PLAN against accepted C1 and owner consolidation scope. Check exact outputs schema/semantic validation, declarative authorization, leaf/scratch versus transport ownership, missing/unsupported grant refusals, resume/settlement custody, and honest per-harness capability standing. Challenge unnecessary blockers or regressions in existing skeptic/commit transport; a future policy join must not cycle or widen absent grants. Verify the first 2-file contract bucket can stand alone and that later tests have precise interfaces/evidence requirements, without demanding future live implementation now. No fileset/whole-lane redesign. Return <=1000-word approve/changes with material reproducible gaps and minimal corrections. Read-only: no source/tests/settings/host/DB/network edits or vendor launches. Help/doc claims in the plan are observations, not a containment certificate.

findings.where: .dev/records/20260906T024750Z-plan-codex-93f60d.json artifacts.PLAN, "Acceptance" paragraph ("artifacts[artifact] must be a bounded single-line handle") and "Proposed catalogue data" (artifact keys plan/skeptic/ruling)
findings.claim: Acceptance binds a fixed envelope artifact key per file entry, but the artifact key is worker-chosen today: jobs.json only says "name that path in artifacts" and never names a key, and measured practice uses five different keys for SKEPTIC.md. Under the proposed rule, 12 of the 13 historical SKEPTIC.md/RULING.md/PLAN.md handles would fail outputs-handle and invalidate. The bucket excludes jobs.json/prompt changes and no slice or dependency owns aligning the worker instruction with the declared key, so the contract lands stating an acceptance rule its own job prompts contradict.

findings.where: .dev/records/20260906T024750Z-plan-codex-93f60d.json artifacts.PLAN, "Grant intersection" ("A file entry permits its declared leaf ... Parent-directory writes are not implicit ... An adapter that needs broader directory rights must refuse this contract") versus "Per-harness evidence" (writable_roots are "additional roots in workspace-write mode")
findings.claim: The contract demands leaf granularity while every mechanism the plan itself measured is directory-granular: codex passes --sandbox workspace-write plus sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=[out], claude passes --add-dir out, grok passes --always-approve. Read literally, all three adapters "need broader directory rights" and must refuse, so the proposed catalogue can never be admitted and the currently working codex check-tests SKEPTIC.md/tmp transport gets no admissible successor. The plan never states whether a mechanism whose enforceable unit is the job out directory (or the declared scratch subtree) is an acceptable over-approximation of G or a refusal; a contract author handed this two-file bucket must invent that rule.

findings.where: .dev/records/20260906T024750Z-plan-codex-93f60d.json artifacts.PLAN, "Acceptance" ("Preserve task/envelope.py as the semantic authority; do not duplicate counts/status/handle rules in a new output validator") and "First ready bucket" ("Dependencies: accepted C1 and the supplied f82853 review, both present")
findings.claim: launch.py never calls envelope.validate — it uses envelope.py only for ENVELOPE_SCHEMA (lines 65 and 743), and its sole validate() call is record.validate. The _handle rule (<=512 chars, single line) is therefore unenforced at collection, which is why this very record's ~13k-character multi-line PLAN artifact closed status ok. So the acceptance rule has no live authority to inherit: implementing it in-bucket is forbidden by the non-duplication sentence, and wiring envelope.validate into launch is outside the bucket, unowned by any slice, and would retroactively invalidate the inline-artifact transport this plan used. The bucket's dependency list omits it, so the contract claims to stand alone on a rule nothing can enforce.

findings.claim: Staleness is the trigger of a non-overridable refusal and an asserted test case ("partial/stale/unsupported capability prevents Popen"), but the plan never defines what makes evidence stale. The probe is said to be "stamped per harness/version/platform/operation" with no date or re-verification window, while docs/verified-couplings.md requires verification stamped "to a version and a date" and voided when a counterparty moves. The dispatch half of the bucket cannot write the refusal predicate, and the independent test author cannot write a red for it, without inventing the freshness rule.

envelope.note:
Changes at 7f56cbb. The artifact under review is the C2 PLAN string in .dev/records/20260906T024750Z-plan-codex-93f60d.json, landed by cdfd11b; 7f56cbb itself adds only .dev/ladder-inputs/scope-launch-c2-plan-review.txt and record 873a3a (git show --stat 7f56cbb). The supplied c06ed944..7f56cbb range carries earlier ladder, discovery and C1 work: context, not this slice.

Verified sound, at HEAD 7f56cbb (git rev-parse HEAD). Measured facts the plan cites hold: jobs.json has zero outputs keys (grep -c '"outputs"' = 0); plan/check-tests/adjudicate demand PLAN.md/SKEPTIC.md/RULING.md in prompt prose only; writable_out is selected by job name at launch 1213 and resume 952, codex check-tests sandbox is forced to workspace-write at 1189-1190, snapshot write bits are stripped and out/tmp assigned as TMPDIR at 958-979. JOBS_PATH (launch.py:30) resolves beside the launcher, not inside the snapshot, so "resolve declarations from the trusted launch-side job catalogue" is already true and resume custody is buildable. Settlement's _invalidate_envelope (1679-1684) is the existing mechanism the plan reuses for outputs-missing/handle/custody, and its git-diff/residual checks genuinely do not prove byte-for-byte immutability, as the plan says.

The proposed JSON Schema is well-formed and does what it claims: the two oneOf branches are disjoint on kind, additionalProperties false on both, #/$defs/path resolves from the root, and the segment grammar ^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]* excludes "." and ".." segments, absolute paths, backslashes, whitespace and globs. Overlap, duplicate-artifact and single-scratch rules are correctly declared as semantic rather than schema checks. Authorization is declarative throughout: no prompt parsing, no job-name branch, "a differently named job with identical declarations gets identical output treatment", empty D yields empty G. The transport reservation list is complete at this ref — out/ holds exactly last-message.json (499, 957, 1814), COMMIT_MSG (1279) and tmp (966); residual.patch lands at job_dir root (1520), not out/. Existing write-job commit transport is preserved explicitly and correctly, and is not regressed: implement declares no outputs, so it gains nothing and loses nothing.

The policy join is consume-only and does not cycle or widen: P is an intersected restriction, C2 defines no profile names and no fallback allow, an unavailable requested decision refuses, and the contract work is stated as not waiting on lane/lane-boundary-20260905. Per-harness standing is honest — all three declared unresolved, chmod and a clean final git diff explicitly refused as prevention, help/version reads called syntax evidence only, and the write-then-restore control named to separate prevention from acceptance detection. Verdict null on the plan itself is the right non-self-approval.

Blockers I probed and did not sustain. Refusing resume of legacy records that would retain an unrecorded grant is a real migration cost for in-flight check-tests jobs, but it is the safe reading and the plan names it. Requiring a capability witness before runtime adoption does not break today's skeptic, because the bucket is contract-only with no runtime change. Retaining exit 3 and deferring reconciliation with docs/wire.md's exit 2 is declared, not smuggled.

Three things do need correcting before this bucket is dispatched, and all are cheap. Name the artifact key rule and where it is enforced, and add prompt/deliverable alignment for the declared key to the adoption dependency list — otherwise the contract's acceptance rule contradicts the instruction workers actually receive (finding 1). Say explicitly whether a directory-granular adapter mechanism scoped to the job out directory or the declared scratch subtree satisfies H, or must refuse; as written the plan's own cited mechanisms all refuse (finding 2). State which component performs handle validation and list the envelope.validate integration as a runtime-adoption dependency, since launch never calls it today (finding 3). The two P3s are a one-line correction each: define staleness with a version-and-date stamp per verified-couplings.md, and fix the test filename to test_record_paths.py.

Could not look: harness versions (codex-cli 0.153.4, Claude Code 2.1.260, Grok 1.0.13 are unverified here — vendor launches, including --version, are outside this job's grant, and the records carry harness.version "unknown"); the two learn.chatgpt.com documentation URLs (no network); ops/bin/suites.sh, live containment, session store. None of these were demanded for a contract-only bucket, and none of the five findings depends on them.
